    StartersMax's sangaSliced pink lamb backstrap, mint mayo, lettuce and tomato on toasted sourdoughHow to make it400g lamb backstrap8 slices of sourdough100g mayonnaise1 bunch mint1 cos lettuce2 tomatoesSear the lamb to pink in a hot pan.Rest, then slice thin.Toast the sourdough. Mix the mayonnaise with chopped mint.Build with crisp cos, ripe tomato and the lamb. When the mutton is nice and lean.Fire Swamp chorizo and hot honeyFlame spurts, quicksand and giant ratsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chorizo fried until crisp and charred, glazed with hot honey and lemon, served sizzling in a pan with crusty bread to mop it up.Slice 2 chorizo sausages (about 300g) into thick rounds on the diagonal.Fry in a dry pan over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp and the oil runs.Add 2 tbsp honey, half a tsp chilli flakes and a squeeze of lemon and toss for 30 seconds until sticky.Scatter with parsley and serve in the pan with a sliced baguette.MainsFezzik's giant pieBeef chuck slow cooked in Worcestershire gravy and baked under pastryHow to make it1.2kg beef chuck2 tbsp plain flour2 brown onions1 bunch thyme2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce600ml beef stock2 sheets of puff pastry1 eggDice the beef and toss with the flour. Slice the onions.Brown the beef in batches.Add the onions and thyme and cook briefly, then add the Worcestershire sauce and stock. Cover and simmer gently until tender and thick.Pour into a large pie dish and cool slightly.Cover with puff pastry, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C.Humperdinck's wedding feast rib roastThe royal wedding, and Inigo's "Prepare to die"How to make itAs written, serves 4Beef rib roast crusted with garlic and herbs, roasted pink and carved at the table, with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes and horseradish cream.Rub a 2kg beef rib roast with salt, pepper, garlic and rosemary and leave uncovered overnight.Roast at 220°C for 20 minutes, then 160°C until 52°C inside, about 60 minutes, and rest 20 minutes.Roast 1kg potatoes.Whisk 140g flour, 3 eggs and 250ml milk, pour into 12 hot oiled muffin holes and bake at 230°C for 20 minutes.Mix 150g sour cream with horseradish.SweetsCliffs of Insanity cakeThree chocolate layers, caramel and rough ganache. He didn't fall? Inconceivable!How to make it350g dark chocolate200g butter4 eggs200g caster sugar200g self-raising flour200g caramels200ml thickened creamMelt part of the chocolate with the butter, whisk in the eggs and sugar, then fold in the flour.Bake in three tins at 170°C.Cool the cakes.Melt the caramels with some of the cream for the filling.Make ganache with the remaining chocolate and cream. Stack tall and spread the ganache roughly over the sides.Miracle pills chocolate trufflesDark chocolate truffles, flaky salt, cocoa. For the mostly dead.How to make it150ml thickened cream250g dark chocolate1 pinch flaky salt3 tbsp cocoaChop the chocolate. Heat the cream and pour over the chocolate with the salt. Stir smooth.Chill until firm.Roll into small balls and coat in cocoa. Have fun storming the castle.DrinksIocane-free spiced grape gobletsWarm red grape juice with cinnamon, star anise, orange peel and honey, no alcoholHow to make it1 L red grape juice1 cinnamon stick2 star anises2 strips of orange peel1 tbsp honeyPut the grape juice, cinnamon stick, star anise, orange peel and honey in a saucepan.Warm gently without boiling, then strain.Serve warm in four goblets, or chill and pour over ice. Set out two goblets each and let someone swap them around while nobody's looking.
